body_markdown:
Earlier in 2026, we had a tremendous amount of fun behind the wheel of[a factory-built, 300-horsepower Ford Maverick](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/factory-tuned-we-drive-fords-800-hp-mustang-700-hp-f-150-and-300-hp-maverick/) . Details about the Ford Maverick SV300T were relatively vague at the time because they were still being finalized, but the truck is now ready to hit showrooms. Ford published full details and pricing for the first Maverick package released through its[Custom Garage](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/mustang-fp800s-turns-up-in-ford-custom-garage/) .


The “SV300T” name wasn’t chosen randomly: It’s a tribute to[the SVT-branded sports cars](https://www.hagerty.com/media/magazine-features/25-greatest-mustangs-2003-svt-cobra-terminator/) that Ford sold decades ago and that have now become sought-after classics. The package gives the Maverick a hot hatch-like 300 horsepower and 350 pound-feet of torque thanks to a turbo sourced from[the Mustang](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2024-ford-mustang-ecoboost-convertible-premium-review-icon-for-a-reason/) , a Ford Racing intercooler, a Borla exhaust, and specific powertrain calibration.


Adding the SV300T Package to the XLT and Lariat trims also brings lowering springs, shocks borrowed from the Maverick Lobo, and what Ford refers to as upgraded stabilizer components. Black or bronze wheels and a graphics package add a finishing touch to the look. The end result is a muscular-looking, street-focused truck that’s quicker than you might expect on an autocross course.


Ford designed the SV300T Package to fit 2025 and 2026 model-year XLT, Lariat, and Lobo models powered by the 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and all-wheel-drive. While that engine comes with a turbo[in its stock configuration](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2027-ford-maverick-pricing-ecoboost-availability-report/) , the Mustang-sourced turbo has a 59-millimeter compressor wheel (up from 53 millimeters). The intercooler also drops peak outlet temperature by 39.6%. Factor in the new calibration, and the 2.0-liter posts increases of 50 horsepower and 70 pound-feet of torque over its stock tune.

The new Ford Maverick SV300T is marketed as a limited-edition model, but there’s no word on how many units will be offered. “We’re intentionally keeping this small,” a Ford spokesperson told *Hagerty* , adding that specific figures aren’t available yet. Pricing depends on how the truck ends up in your garage (you have two options to choose from) and which trim level you select.


If you want a turnkey truck, you can use Ford’s so-called “Easy Button” and add the package to the XLT trim for $ 15,595 or to the Lobo trim for $13,395. Those figures include the recommended tires, installation, and transportation. Alternatively, buyers can order the parts as a kit and have them installed by the ASE-certified technician of their choice. The kits start at $6075 for the XLT and $4500 for the Lobo. The latter is less expensive because it already features the upgraded suspension parts.


Options include two-piston front calipers for the XLT and Lariat trims. The kit is sold directly by Ford, so it’s covered by a three-year, 36,000-mile warranty plan that starts on the vehicle’s in-service date. Ford wants to position its Custom Garage builds as alternatives to aftermarket tuning packages, and the factory warranty should play a significant role in giving buyers peace of mind. There’s a catch: Ford confirmed to *Hagerty* that the Maverick SV300T is not legal in California.
